column1: # The opam set's programs judged by their own verdict (the user's decision of 2026-11-07: a test's own verdict wherever it has one,
# "the testsuite programs' assert and exit status"; doc/ocaml/OCAML-SURVEY.md, "As built: the opam set's own verdicts"), read by
# bin/oi's own_verdicts at check time. ID<TAB>STATUS<TAB>KIND<TAB>ARG<TAB>WHY, KIND:
#   status  the exit status alone: a package's test as its own build runs it (topkg's Pkg.test, b0's B0_ocaml.test: the runner
#           fails on a non-zero exit, the output is the test's log, not compared)
#   file    the exit status and ARG's bytes, ARG a file of test/ocaml/opam/ written from the program's own text (load.ml)
#   empty   the exit status and no output (a program whose text runs nothing that prints, as ocamltest's missing reference)
#   golden  the exit status and ARG's bytes as `file`, ARG a golden file of test/ocaml/opam/golden/: the program's standard output and
#           error merged as the harness writes them, written from its text and the library's source before any comparison and
#           reviewed in test/ocaml/opam/golden.edn (the user's decision of 2026-11-20: reviewed golden files, JCS361 (a)'s way); bin/oi's
#           own_verdicts refuses a golden line without its review (or whose review gives another status or file) and a review
# The demonstrations their packages do not run as tests (pprint's PPrintTest, cmdliner's examples, blueprints and test_shell,
# ~run:false in cmdliner's B0.ml) were judged by the recorded runs until 2026-11-20; their golden lines since. A program not listed
# is judged by the recorded run: none is now, every opam program of the corpus has a line here.
